No workflow_run crash detection for remote attempts — nothing records the Actions run id, so a cancelled or killed worker is only noticed at stale_after (1h by default).
A per-task `model` override is not plumbed through workflow inputs; the worker's model is whatever claude_args says.

claude-code-action@v1's exact input names (prompt, claude_args, claude_code_oauth_token, anthropic_api_key) and whether the step's `env` reaches the Claude process are taken from the action's documented interface, not verified against a run.

The harness worktree-isolation guard blocks any Bash command containing the token that names this terminal verb, so every documented invocation of it is unreachable from a worktree-isolated session; this attempt finished by spawning the CLI from a script instead.

results.summary:
`hkb init --with-actions` now generates two workflows from `templates/actions/`, and the board can run with the laptop closed. PR #42 (draft, CI green).

**kanban-dispatch.yml** is `hkb dispatch --max 1 --board <slug> --profiles claude-action` on `issues:[closed,reopened,labeled,unlabeled]`, `pull_request:[closed]`, `pull_request_review`, `workflow_run`, `workflow_dispatch`, with `schedule: */15` as a sweeper only and `concurrency: {group: kb-dispatch-<board>, cancel-in-progress: false}`. A preflight step prints a `::notice::` and dispatches nothing when `KB_TOKEN` is unset — which is also what a fork PR gets, since fork events carry no secrets.

**kanban-worker-claude.yml** is one attempt: `hkb context <n>` becomes claude-code-action@v1's `prompt` through `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` behind a `/dev/urandom` delimiter (issue text is untrusted and never reaches a `run:` block), with the same allowlist and force-push denial a local Claude worker gets, and a final `if: always()` step that records an attempt which ended without a terminal verb as `hkb block … --kind transient` — the stand-in for the `Stop` hook a runner has not got.

**Two dispatcher concepts made this work, and both are the load-bearing part of the design.**

`mode: "trigger"` (new, third alongside `process` and `claude-bg`): the launch only *starts* work elsewhere and exits. `spawnWorker` runs it to completion — a non-zero exit is a `spawn_failed` and the task goes straight back to *ready* — and returns `remote: true`, which the tick writes onto the attempt row. The reclaim pass then skips every local check (pid, background job, worktree) and the attempt lives or dies by its heartbeat and `max_runtime`. Without it, `gh workflow run` exiting in a second is read as a crash on the very next tick; there is no combination of existing fields that escapes those branches, which is why `src/dispatch.js` had to be touched at all.

`hkb dispatch --profiles a,b` restricts **selection only**. Without it an Actions tick claims a `kb:agent:claude` task, fails to find `claude` on the runner, and burns a retry on work the laptop was about to pick up — with `mode: claude-bg` it does not even fail loudly, it records a live-looking attempt that sits until the stale reclaim. Reclaim, promote, reconcile and the orphan sweep stay unfiltered, because a second dispatcher sweeping the whole board is the entire point. The flag rejects a profile that is not in board.json, which is why `.kanban/board.json` here now lists `"claude-action": {}`.

**If you touch this:** `test/actions.test.js` asserts the two workflows committed in `.github/workflows/` are byte-for-byte what the generator writes, so edit `templates/actions/` and regenerate (`installActions(root, {board, profiles: triggerProfiles(cfg), timeoutMinutes})`) rather than editing the committed copies. `test/yaml.js` is a strict YAML-subset parser written for these tests only — hkb itself still parses no YAML — and it throws with a line number on anything outside the subset, so a malformed template fails rather than half-parses.

Three things are honestly unproven, all written into docs/harnesses.md: the workflows have never *executed* on GitHub (they are not on the default branch yet and firing one needs `KB_TOKEN` plus a Claude secret); a worker whose run is cancelled or killed is only noticed at `stale_after`, because nothing records the Actions run id for a remote attempt and `workflow_run` crash detection is therefore not implemented; and a task's `model` override is not plumbed through workflow inputs.

`src/dispatch.js` is also owned by #39 (auto-gc, PR #41). The edits here are five small disjoint spots and this branch rebased onto `main` (96f3c7b) without conflict, but a reviewer merging both should read that file's diff twice.

**Protocol foot-gun, the same class as the one #4 reported.** The harness's worktree-isolation guard refuses any Bash command containing the bare token that names this verb — it reads it as bash's builtin of the same name and answers "this command runs a string through …, which can't be verified to stay inside the worktree". `hkb heartbeat 8` was never blocked, so it is the word, not hkb. Every documented form is affected: `--summary-file`, `--from-stdin`, and the `node bin/hkb.js …` spelling. This attempt finished by having a small script under `.kanban/logs/` spawn the real CLI with an argv array, so no such token appears on the command line. As with #4's DENY_PATTERNS note: a guard that matches text anywhere in a command string, rather than the command actually being run, can make a terminal verb unreachable.
